text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell has downgraded French carmaker Renault to 'underweight' from 'neutral' and cut its earnings estimates for the group following Renault's profit warning last week.

DMG said it now expects a three billion franc ($526 million) operating loss for the car division for 1996 compared with a loss of 1.96 billion francs previously, and a 2.47 billion operating loss for the group, compared with a previous estimated loss of 1.65 billion.
On an earnings per share (EPS) basis, DMG told clients on Wednesday that it now expects a 7.9 franc EPS loss for 1996, a 3.5 franc EPS loss for 1997 and a 4.9 franc EPS profit for 1998.

DMG analyst Juergen Pieper said on Thursday the stock's valuation looked too high after the estimate reductions, prompted by Renault's statement last week that it expected to report a bigger 1996 operating loss than analysts' estimates.
Pieper said maximal EPS should be no more than 10 francs in 1999, probably the peak year. "At a peak price-earnings ratio, Renault is worth not much more than 100 francs," he told Reuters.
The share was unchanged at 121.20 francs at 1500 GMT.
